title: Legislative districts of Bulacan
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Bulacan''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Bulacan]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Bulacan's 1st congressional district|first]], [[Bulacan's 2nd congressional district|second]], [[Bulacan's 3rd congressional district|third]], [[Bulacan's 4th congressional district|fourth]], [[Bulacan's 5th congressional district|fifth]] and [[Bulacan's 6th congressional district|sixth]] congressional districts. [[File:Bulacan Congressional Districts 2022.svg|thumb|Congressional districts of Bulacan.]] [[Valenzuela, Metro Manila|Valenzuela]] (formerly Polo), now a [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]], was last represented as part of the province in 1972. The component city of [[San Jose del Monte]], while remaining an integral part of the province, was granted separate congressional representation in 2003. == History == Bulacan as initially composed of one representative district, wherein it elected [[#1898–1899|four representatives, at large]], to the [[Malolos Congress]] in [[1898 Philippine legislative election|1898]]; this lasted until 1899. It was later divided into two representative districts in 1907 for the [[Philippine Assembly]].{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=1582|date=January 9, 1907|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5054|title=An Act to Provide for the Holding of Elections in the Philippine Islands, for the Organization of the Philippine Assembly, and for Other Purposes|accessdate=September 4, 2022}} When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the province formed part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Third District|third senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] represented the province in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, the province retained its two pre-war representative districts. [[Valenzuela, Metro Manila|Valenzuela]], then a municipality, was separated from Bulacan to form the [[Metro Manila|Metropolitan Manila Area]] on November 7, 1975, by virtue of Presidential Decree No. 824.{{cite PH act|chamber=PD|number=824|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/presdecs/pd1975/pd_824_1975.html|date=November 7, 1975|access-date=August 26, 2019|title=Creating the Metropolitan Manila and the Metropolitan Manila Commission and for Other Purposes|website=The LawPHiL Project}} Afterwards, the reduced province of Bulacan was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region III]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#1984–1986|four representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. The province was reapportioned into four [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=August 26, 2019}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 9230.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9230|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_12/RA09230.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629110211/http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_12/RA09230.pdf|date=December 18, 2003|website=[[Congress of the Philippines]]|title=An Act amending section 10(b) and section 58 of Republic Act No. 8797, otherwise known as "An Act converting the municipality of San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan into a component city to be known as the city of San Jose Del Monte" and providing funds therefor|access-date=August 26, 2019|archive-date=June 29, 2011}} on December 18, 2003, separated from the [[Bulacan's 4th congressional district|fourth]] district the city of [[San Jose del Monte]], which first elected its [[Legislative district of San Jose del Monte|separate representative]] beginning in the [[2004 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2004 elections]]. However, for the purposes of electing [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] members, the city remains part of the province's [[Bulacan Provincial Board#4th District|4th Sangguniang Panlalawigan District]].{{cite web|url=http://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2007/01/com_res_7801annex-_b.pdf|title=COMELEC Resolution No. 7801 – Annex B|access-date=August 26, 2019|date=January 11, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080530152815/http://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2007/01/com_res_7801annex-_b.pdf|archive-date=May 30, 2008|url-status=dead|author=Commission on Elections|author-link=Commission on Elections (Philippines)}} Republic Act No. 9591,{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9591|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209591.pdf|website=[[Senate of the Philippines]]|author=Congress of the Philippines|author-link=Congress of the Philippines|date=May 1, 2009|access-date=August 26, 2019|title=An Act amending Section 57 of Republic Act No. 8754, otherwise known as the Charter of the City of Malolos}} approved on May 1, 2009, sought to separate the city of [[Malolos]] from the [[Bulacan's 1st congressional district|first district]] to form its own congressional district starting in the 2010 elections. Like in the case of San Jose del Monte, the residents of Malolos would have remained as part of the province's [[Bulacan Provincial Board#1st District|1st Sangguniang Panlalawigan district]]. However, on January 25, 2010, the Supreme Court declared the creation of the Legislative District of Malolos as unconstitutional, citing that the city's population at the time did not meet the minimum 250,000 count required by the constitution.{{cite PH act|chamber=GR|number=188078|title= VICTORINO B. ALDABA, CARLO JOLETTE S. FAJARDO, JULIO G. MORADA, and MINERVA ALDABA MORADA, Petitioners, v. COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS, Respondent.|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/cralaw/2010januarydecisions.php?id=1345|website=Chan Robles Law Library|access-date=August 26, 2019|author=Supreme Court of the Philippines|author-link=Supreme Court of the Philippines|date=January 25, 2010}} Malolos today remains part of the first district. Republic Act No. 11546,{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11546|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2021/05/26/republic-act-no-11546/|website=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]]|author=Congress of the Philippines|author-link=Congress of the Philippines|date=August 13, 2021|access-date=August 13, 2021|title=An Act Reapportioning the Province of Bulacan into Six (6) Legislative Districts}} approved on May 26, 2021, reapportioned Bulacan into six congressional districts. *1st District: Malolos, Bulakan, Calumpit, Hagonoy, Paombong, Pulilan *2nd District: Baliwag, Bustos, Plaridel *3rd District: Doña Remedios Trinidad, San Ildefonso, San Miguel, San Rafael *4th District: Meycauayan, Marilao, Obando *5th District: Balagtas, Bocaue, Guiguinto, Pandi *6th District: Angat, Norzagaray, Santa Maria == Current districts == The province was last redistricted in 2021, wherein the province gained two seats in the house.
